t:
Section 412 (relating to minimum funding standards) is amended—

    (1) 
in subsection (b), by striking out “(40 plan years in the case of a multiemployer plan)” and “(20 plan years in the case of a multiemployer plan)” each place they appear;
 
    (2) 
by adding at the end of subsection (b) the following new paragraphs:

“(6) Certain amortization charges and credits.—In the case of a plan which, immediately before the date of the enactment of the Multiemployer Pension Plan Amendments Act of 1980, was a multiemployer plan (within the meaning of section 414(f) as in effect immediately before such date)—
“(A) any amount described in paragraph (2)(B)(ii), (2)(B)(iii), or (3)(B)(i) of this subsection which arose in a plan year beginning before such date shall be amortized in equal annual installments (until fully amortized) over 40 plan years, beginning with the plan year in which the amount arose;
“(B) any amount described in paragraph (2)(B)(iv) or (3)(B)(ii) of this subsection which arose in a plan year beginning before such date shall be amortized in equal annual installments (until fully amortized) over 20 plan years, beginning with the plan year in which the amount arose;
“(C) any change in past service liability which arises during the period of 3 plan years beginning on or after such date, and results from a plan amendment adopted before such date, shall be amortized in equal annual installments (until fully amortized) over 40 plan years, beginning with the plan year in which the change arises; and
“(D) any change in past service liability which arises during the period of 2 plan years beginning on or after such date, and results from the changing of a group of participants from one benefit level to another benefit level under a schedule of plan benefits which—
“(i) was adopted before such date, and
“(ii) was effective for any plan participant before the beginning of the first plan year beginning on or after such date,
shall be amortized in equal annual installments (until fully amortized) over 40 plan years, beginning with the plan year in which the change arises.



“(7) 
Special rules for multiemployer plans.—
For purposes of this section—

“(A) 
Withdrawal liability.—Any amount received by a multiemployer plan in payment of all or part of an employer’s withdrawal liability under part 1 of subtitle E of title IV of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 shall be considered an amount contributed by the employer to or under the plan. The Secretary may prescribe by regulation additional charges and credits to a multiemployer plan’s funding standard account to the extent necessary to prevent withdrawal liability payments from being unduly reflected as advance funding for plan liabilities.

“(B) 
Adjustments when a multiemployer plan leaves reorganization.—If a multiemployer plan is not in reorganization in the plan year but was in reorganization in the immediately preceding plan year, any balance in the funding standard account at the close of such immediately preceding plan year—
“(i) shall be eliminated by an offsetting credit or charge (as the case may be), but
“(ii) shall be taken into account in subsequent plan years by being amortized in equal annual installments (until fully amortized) over 30 plan years.
The preceding sentence shall not apply to the extent of any accumulated funding deficiency under section 418B(a) as of the end of the last plan year that the plan was in reorganization.

“(C) Plan payments to supplemental program or withdrawal liability payment fund.—Any amount paid by a plan during a plan year to the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation pursuant to section 4222 of such Act or to a fund exempt under section 501(c)(22) pursuant to section 4223 of such Act shall reduce the amount of contributions considered received by the plan for the plan year.
“(D) Interim withdrawal liability payments.—Any amount paid by an employer pending a final determination of the employer’s withdrawal liability under part 1 of subtitle E of title IV of such Act and subsequently refunded to the employer by the plan shall be charged to the funding standard account in accordance with regulations prescribed by the Secretary.
“(E) For purposes of the full funding limitation under subsection (c)(7), unless otherwise provided by the plan, the accrued liability under a multiemployer plan shall not include benefits which are not nonforfeitable under the plan after the termination of the plan (taking into consideration section 411(d)(3)).”; and  
    (3) 
by adding at the end thereof the following new subsection:


“(j)
Certain Terminated Multiemployer Plans.—This section applies with respect to a terminated multiemployer plan to which section 4021 of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 applies, until the last day of the plan year in which the plan terminates, within the meaning of section 4041A(a)(2) of that Act. 


“(k) 
Financial Assistance.—Any amount of any financial assistance from the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation to any plan, and any repayment of such amount, shall be taken into account under this section in such manner as determined by the Secretary.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that this is a purely technical tax amendment on pension funding with no outside-party process, so the answer should be No. However, the section authorizes the Secretary to prescribe regulations, and under the definition a grant of rulemaking authority counts as participation, even when discretionary ("may"), because rulemaking brings in public comment. The word "participants" elsewhere in the section refers to plan participants and is not the basis for the label.
fable.s: The Secretary may prescribe by regulation additional charges and credits to a multiemployer plan’s funding standard account to the extent necessary to prevent withdrawal liability payments from being unduly reflected as advance funding for plan liabilities.

qwen_block.w: This section primarily amends technical provisions regarding minimum funding standards for multiemployer pension plans. While it grants the Secretary authority to prescribe regulations, it does not explicitly require public comment, hearings, or consultation with outside parties in the text provided. The definition of participation requires explicit mechanisms for outside involvement (like comment periods or advisory boards with non-federal members). Mere regulatory authority without specified participatory procedures is not sufficient to label as 'Yes' under the conservative interpretation, especially given the technical nature of the amendments. The 'tempting' reading might be that regulation implies participation, but the text itself does not mandate it.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary may prescribe by regulation additional charges and credits to a multiemployer plan’s funding standard account to the extent necessary to prevent withdrawal liability payments from being unduly reflected as advance funding for plan liabilities.

opus.w: This section lets the Secretary prescribe regulations, and charges are also applied "in accordance with regulations prescribed by the Secretary." Under the DEFINITION and Example 6, authority to make rules counts as participation even when it is optional, because rulemaking brings in public comment. It is tempting to answer "No" because the section is mostly technical amortization rules with no explicit hearing or consultation, but the grant of rulemaking authority is enough.
opus.s: The Secretary may prescribe by regulation additional charges and credits to a multiemployer plan’s funding standard account to the extent necessary to prevent withdrawal liability payments from being unduly reflected as advance funding for plan liabilities.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through.** The section is mostly technical pension-funding arithmetic: amortization periods and how withdrawal-liability payments are credited. It never mentions comment periods, hearings, or outside consultation, so "No" is tempting. But subsection (b)(7)(A) gives the Secretary rulemaking authority. Under the DEFINITION, "requiring rulemaking" counts as participation, and Example 6 shows that optional authority ("may by regulation") counts too.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the Secretary to prescribe regulations regarding pension funding calculations. It does not require consultation with outside parties, public hearings, or comment periods for these specific technical regulations. The authority to regulate is internal to the agency's decision-making process unless a specific participatory mechanism is mandated.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary may prescribe by regulation additional charges and credits to a multiemployer plan’s funding standard account to the extent necessary to prevent withdrawal liability payments from being unduly reflected as advance funding for plan liabilities.
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it mentions the Secretary prescribing regulations, which might involve public comment.
Resolution: The text only authorizes the Secretary to prescribe regulations for technical accounting purposes (funding standard accounts). It does not explicitly require a public comment period, hearing, or consultation with outside parties for these specific regulations. Mere authority to regulate is not participation unless the process of regulation (like notice-and-comment) is specified or implied by a general rulemaking requirement in the section, which is absent here. The focus is on internal accounting adjustments for pension plans.
